chain.title: Knapped From a Rock
chain.desc: Nine stone shards from a handful of cobblestone; the Stone Age tier opens here and needs no tools at all.

chain.title: The First Thing You Swing
chain.desc: Two stone shards in an L; the cheapest weapon in a mod of 561 items.

chain.title: Sharpened Bone
chain.desc: Two bones set diagonally, the other half of the twelve-recipe Stone Age tier.

chain.title: Hide Over the Head
chain.desc: The Stone Age headpiece; the rest of the caveman set is the same idea in three more shapes.

chain.title: The Tool That Makes Tools
chain.desc: Stone tool material over a stick. Every metal blank in the mod is made by holding this hammer in the grid, so nothing past the Stone Age happens without it.

chain.title: Nine Stone, One Blank
chain.desc: A full grid of stone yields nine blank templates; these are stonecut into the shape templates and also act as the addition in every part-smithing recipe.

chain.title: Cut to a Shape
chain.desc: A stonecutter turns a blank template into a shape template - one of thirty-seven such cuts, one per weapon and tool family.

chain.title: Iron, Beaten Small
chain.desc: An iron ingot worked with the hammer; the smallest of the five blank sizes that determine which weapons a metal can become.

chain.title: Iron, Beaten Large
chain.desc: Blanks step up through small and medium to large and huge; a broadsword needs large, a claymore or cleaver needs huge.

chain.title: Pressed Into a Blade
chain.desc: Smithing table: broadsword template, a large iron blank as the base, a blank template as the addition. Immersive Engineering and Energized Power metal presses are optional alternate routes to the same part.

chain.title: A Blade on a Haft
chain.desc: The part over any wooden stick. Every one of the mod's twenty-nine metal weapon families is assembled exactly this way.

chain.title: Edo Steel
chain.desc: The Edo Period tier: katana, wakizashi and ninjato, all from large or medium blanks through their own templates.

chain.title: Over the Gunwale
chain.desc: The Piracy tier's signature tool, alongside the cutlass-adjacent saber and the harpoon.

chain.title: A Haft That Won't Splinter
chain.desc: Two iron ingots stacked; the metal handle the batons, nunchucks and longsticks are built on.

chain.title: Rabbit Hide and String
chain.desc: Four cloth per craft; it backs every piece of the mod's five armour sets.

chain.title: Plate for a Uniform
chain.desc: Pressed from a tiny iron blank, or hammered by hand; the armor_plates/iron tag it fills is what the soldier set actually reads.

chain.title: The Early Modern Head
chain.desc: Three iron plates over two cloth. The Early Modern Age tier is where armour and firearms arrive together.

chain.title: Drawn Back Further
chain.desc: The mod's own bow line, and the required base for the compound bow that follows it.

chain.title: Cams and Cable
chain.desc: Wooden sticks braced around a recurve bow; the deepest bow in the mod.

chain.title: Modern Age Opens Loud
chain.desc: The base thrown explosive; frag, cluster, smoke and poison variants all branch off this tier.

chain.title: Sealed Head
chain.desc: The heaviest armour the mod ships, and the last set before the Future tier stops using plate at all.

chain.title: Amethyst Under Blaze Powder
chain.desc: An amethyst cluster ringed with blaze powder; it fills the forge:gems/energy tag and gates the entire Future tier.

chain.title: Netherite Around a Crystal
chain.desc: Netherite ingots, a blue dye and an energy crystal; the four colours and their double-bladed forms are all the same shape.

chain.title: The Template, As Vanilla Intended
chain.desc: A vanilla Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template on the diamond weapon - the mod reuses vanilla's own netherite step rather than inventing one.

chain.title: Left in the Stronghold
chain.desc: No recipe exists for it anywhere. It is injected into stronghold corridor and crossing chests, alongside six other named blades.

notes: Forge, 1.20.1, confirmed from META-INF/mods.toml (modId "ageofweapons", loaderVersion [46,), minecraft [1.20,1.20.3), optional majruszsdifficulty; no fabric.mod.json). The Modrinth listing shows forge and neoforge on older files but this newest 1.20.1 build is forge-only. ID SET. 603 model/item stems intersect with 610 item.ageofweapons.<name> lang keys to give 561 items - unusually, lang is LARGER than models here because the mod also names items it renders from a shared parent. 9 blocks each carry both a blockstate and a block.ageofweapons.<name> key. Verified set = 570. No widening was needed. NBT-VARIANT CHECK - THE OPPOSITE OF TACZ. Every weapon is a separate registered item id. The mod's shape is family x material: 29 metal weapon families each ship six material variants and six matching _part items, giving roughly 350 of the 561 ids, and each one has its own model, lang key, recipe file and data/ageofweapons/capabilities/weapons/<id>.json stat file. Nothing is a shared id with a tag, so plain-id wheels are correct and were used. OBTAINABILITY - 9 DROPPED. ageofweapons:handle, shears_template, weapon_box_1, weapon_box_2, weapon_box_3, nexus_blue, nexus_green, nexus_red and nexus_yellow are registered but produced by no recipe and named in no loot table. The four nexus blocks and three weapon boxes belong to the mod's arena/minigame side (itemGroup lang confirms a minigame tab) and are placed by an operator, not earned. All nine are excluded. LOOT-ONLY ITEMS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. The seven named blades - excalibur, master_sword, buster_sword, titan_sword, sword_of_kings, elucidator, nightmare_scythe - have no recipe of any type. Their source is data/ageofweapons/loot_tables/inject/stronghold_corridor.json and inject/stronghold_crossing.json, which list all seven. That is a real, verified source, so they are questable and form the fourth wheel. ORDERING comes from the mod's own recipe folder taxonomy, which is an explicit age ladder: weapons/stone_age (12 recipes), weapons/antiquity (29), weapons/middle_ages (105), weapons/edo_period (35), weapons/piracy (36), weapons/early_modern_age (30), weapons/modern_age (16), weapons/future (19), plus weapons/vanilla and weapons/fantasy as cross-cutting sets. The chain walks that ladder. The crafting spine underneath it is uniform and was read from parts/** and weapons/**: hammer -> <size>_<material>_blank -> smithing_transform with a shape template and a blank_template addition -> <weapon>_<material>_part -> crafting_shaped with a stick -> the weapon; netherite weapons are then a vanilla netherite_upgrade_smithing_template on the diamond weapon. COMPAT RECIPES ARE NOT REQUIRED. 426 of the 1172 recipe files sit under compat/energized_power and compat/immersive_engineering and are metal_press duplicates of the parts recipes, every one guarded by a forge:mod_loaded condition. The smithing route in parts/** is the vanilla-only path and is what the chain assumes, so no chain step depends on another mod being installed. ARMOUR RULE APPLIED. Only helmets are quested (caveman, soldier, mech suit); the soldier set's other three pieces plus the other four helmets sit in one wheel, and no lone chestplate, leggings or boots quest was emitted. Every _slab, _stairs, _wall, _trim and stripped_ id is excluded - this mod ships none of those anyway. Seven wheels sized 13, 13, 9, 6, 8, 8 and 8. The chain is 25 steps against 570 ids because the mod's real depth is width, not length: it repeats one crafting spine across eight ages, six materials and twenty-nine families, so the wheels carry the breadth and the chain carries the ladder.
